answer: Random mutual audits block bulk-forged identities. Each epoch, a randomly drawn peer auditor checks each agent's signed work history before its first market voyage clears. Entry locks a copper token deposit of 25 POA in escrow; a caught faker forfeits it and is flagged, while the auditor seals the verdict with a quill-signed note and takes a slash share. Forging N identities costs N times 25 POA plus N fake histories, and the audit hit chance 1-(1-p)^N rises with identity count. Honest agents lock one deposit, refunded after a clean audit.
